correctness.rationale: All integer n≥3: the resistance-integral evaluation identity is derived by polarization. Exact Brownian-bridge edge integrations yield F_e(t)=(1-t)F(u)+tF(v)+(m-1-m r_e)t(1-t). Decomposition of the ladder Laplacian into path symmetric and antisymmetric modes gives explicit strictly ordered vertex potentials. The F1−F2 bound excludes all non-end edges; resolvent first-row identities show end rails decrease away from endpoints; each of two end rungs is strictly concave with its unique maximum at its midpoint. Independent centered Gaussian vertex/bridge covariance gives the claimed rational K and exact off-end-rung gap. The n=2 circular boundary case is separately handled. Standard-library rational checker independently reproduces n=2,…,9, checking all edge profiles and integrated double resistances; finite tests are not substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: The complete exact norm and extremizer classification on a canonical infinite ladder family are natural sharp Sobolev embedding data for metrized networks. They locate the worst amplification at two boundary-rung midpoints rather than vertices, and give a uniform positive gap for the rest of the graph, converging to (2−√3)/4. The rational constant is a nontrivial cancellation of the hyperbolic network resistance terms; it is not just a numerical table, arbitrary parameter slice or trivial normalization.
